articles.description:
AI Genesis: Building Neural Networks from Random Noise


Tired of painstakingly crafting every layer of your deep learning models? What if instead of architecting, you could grow neural networks from scratch? Imagine starting with a single computational 'cell' and letting it self-organize into a functional network, driven by nothing but random noise. 
The core concept is surprisingly simple: inject controlled noise into an initial layer of artificial neurons. This noise acts as a 'seed' pattern, causing the neurons to spontaneously activate in a structured way. A second layer of neurons then learns this emergent pattern through a simple, local connection adjustment rule. This creates organized layers, mimicking biological brain development.
I've found this approach yields some fascinating …
articles.title: AI Genesis: Building Neural Networks from Random Noise

This guide provides a step-by-step technical walkthrough for migrating a .NET application from MediatR to LiteBus. It maps MediatR's concepts directly to their LiteBus equivalents, focusing on code and configuration changes.
Since MediatR is shifting to a commercial model, LiteBus offers a powerful, free, and open-source alternative with a more ambitious feature set.
The primary difference between the two libraries is their approach to abstractions:
  MediatR uses a generic IRequest<TResponse> for both commands and queries.
  LiteBus provides distinct ICommand<TResult>, IQuery<TResult>, and IEvent interfaces.
This semantic distinction in LiteBus enforces Command Query Separation (CQS) at the compiler level, making your application's intent clearer.
